issues.detail: Missing error handling and debugging guidance for common training failures (OOM errors, convergence problems, divergence) and evaluation beyond eval_loss metrics.
Tightly coupled to Hugging Face ecosystem (transformers, PEFT, TRL libraries); NVIDIA GPU with CUDA is a hard requirement with only secondary mention of GGUF export for portability.

scenarios.name: qlora-on-limited-vram
scenarios.rationale: Response A implements all three rubric requirements exactly: BitsAndBytesConfig with load_in_4bit=True and nf4, quantization_config and device_map in model_init_kwargs, and SFTConfig with per_device_train_batch_size=2 and gradient_checkpointing=True. Response B configures BitsAndBytesConfig correctly but fails the other two: it passes quantization_config/device_map directly to from_pretrained (not in model_init_kwargs), uses standard Trainer/TrainingArguments instead of SFTTrainer/SFTConfig, sets per_device_train_batch_size=4 (exceeds ≤2 requirement), and omits gradient_checkpointing entirely.

scenarios.name: conversational-assistant-only-loss
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly implements all three rubric requirements (assistant_only_loss=True, messages format, LoraConfig with task_type=CAUSAL_LM) with specific, runnable code; Response A shows conceptual mastery but omits the exact API parameters, never mentioning assistant_only_loss=True and only showing LoraConfig in a secondary 'manual' approach.

scenarios.name: merge-and-export-gguf
scenarios.rationale: Response B meets all 5 rubric requirements exactly (16-bit dtype, PeftModel.from_pretrained, merge_and_unload, saved tokenizer, convert_hf_to_gguf.py), while Response A uses 'auto' precision instead of explicit 16-bit and substitutes convert.py instead of the specified convert_hf_to_gguf.py script.
